chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Jabbo Smith: after-hours in Chicago and the rival of Louis
summary: Milt recalls late nights with Jabbo Smith, and Danny, who went to Europe with Jabbo, praises him as a fearless challenger of Louis.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah. My favorite was Jabbo Smith then in Chicago. When Louis left, he took his band. I was trying to play at 1:30 or 2, and Jabbo came in. And we would take out tips that we had made from the night, call up some lady that had a nice apartment or flat, and when we got off we'd
all go up there, and she'd have the chicken and whiskey, and we'd sit right up there all evening, you know, until daylight, havin' us a ball.
I went to Europe with Jabbo.

Mmm-hmm. And Ron Elliott(?)...See, Jabbo didn't know me. So I went on to tell him, give him some courage, because he was kind of down, see. [CHEWING, INAUDIBLE SENTENCE] And I went on to tell them how important Jabbo was and what a great trumpet player he was, and he was a rival of Louis. Because at this (?) his lip was done, and he stayed off to himself, which he ....(?). But this guy can play, man. When his lip got up, that band went to Europe, he was something else. But Ron Elliott(?) looked at him like Jabbo, Jabbo wasn't... But none of them could understand....
He was fantastic. When I played with him back in the Thirties, I had never heard anything like that. It was like listening to Charlie Shavers and somebody who had that...
He had a thing of his own, and a rivalry with Louis. He had nerve enough to challenge Louis.
I don't know about the ballad. But this man was fantastic.
